skill.name: agent-fs
skill.description: Use when the user wants to store, retrieve, search, or manage files in agent-fs — an agent-first filesystem backed by S3. Triggers on: "save this to agent-fs", "find that file", "store this document", "search agent-fs", "list my files", "show version history", "revert file", "set up agent-fs", "get a signed url", "share this file", "manage members", "invite user", "list members", "remove member", "update role", "reset api key", "rotate api key", "lost my api key", file persistence for agents, shared agent filesystem, or any mention of the agent-fs CLI. Also use when the user needs to manage drives, manage org/drive members, generate presigned URLs, check recent activity, or use semantic search across stored files. Also use when the user wants to run SQL over stored data files ("query this csv", "sql over my files", "duckdb", "aggregate the parquet file", "query the sqlite db", "join these spreadsheets"). Also use when the user wants to mount or unmount agent-fs as a Linux FUSE filesystem ("mount agent-fs", "fuse mount", "fuse", "remote mount", "sandbox mount", "expose drives as files", "use cat/grep/mv on my agent-fs files", "umount the drive", "mount a remote drive", "mount from sprite", "mount from e2b", "mount from hetzner"). Also use when the user wants to use agent-fs as a just-bash filesystem. Also use when the user wants to set up agent-fs without Docker or S3 ("local filesystem backend", "filesystem storage", "no docker", "onboard --filesystem", "store files on disk"). If the user mentions agent-fs in any context, always consult this skill.
skill.summary: Manage versioned files, search stored documents, and query data through the agent-fs CLI.
skill.author: desplega-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown delimiters, documented application operations, or scoped authentication examples rather than malicious behavior. Six findings identify risky FUSE permission changes and forced system configuration replacement; one additional finding covers S3 credentials exposed through command arguments. No evidence found of prompt injection or intentional credential exfiltration; external CLI implementations were not included in this review.

remediation.issue: The sandbox example grants every local user read and write access to the FUSE device.
remediation.suggestion: Check existing device permissions first and use narrowly scoped group or device access instead of unconditional chmod 666.

remediation.issue: The setup force-replaces /etc/mtab without checking the existing system configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect the existing mount-table configuration and modify it only when required, with explicit administrator approval and a recovery plan.

remediation.issue: The example enables user_allow_other globally even though its mount command does not request shared access.
remediation.suggestion: Omit this setting by default and require explicit approval when sharing mounts with other local users is necessary.

remediation.issue: Custom S3 onboarding passes access credentials through command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a supported protected credential input and warn against exposing keys through process listings, shell history, or agent transcripts.

content.value_statement: Agent workflows need persistent files that remain searchable and traceable across changes. This skill guides agent-fs operations for storage, search, version history, collaboration, and SQL queries.
actual_capabilities: Guide text and binary uploads, downloads, file edits, and organization or drive selection.
Inspect version history, compare stored versions, and restore files on supported backends.
Choose regex, full-text, hybrid, or semantic search within the active drive.
Query stored CSV, Parquet, spreadsheet, JSON, SQLite, and DuckDB data with SQL.
Manage comments, notifications, drive membership, and backend-specific sharing links.
Explain local or remote Linux FUSE mounting and the just-bash filesystem adapter.
limitations: The skill supplies documentation, not the agent-fs executable, service, or storage infrastructure.
Semantic results require configured embeddings; search may return keyword-only results without them.
FUSE requires Linux, device access, and system capabilities; its setup examples need administrator security review.
Local-backend sharing links require sign-in and do not expire; S3 presigned links are public bearer links until expiration.

use_cases.title: Persist Agent Project Files
use_cases.description: Store project documents, check the target drive, and track revisions with version messages and concurrency checks.

use_cases.title: Analyze Stored Business Data
use_cases.description: Join stored datasets and summarize results with DuckDB while checking row limits and truncation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Shared Documents
use_cases.description: Review comments, inspect recent activity, and manage approved drive memberships with explicit roles.

prompt_templates.title: List Files in a Drive
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my current agent-fs organization and drive, then list files under [folder]. Do not change anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect stored files and confirm context.

prompt_templates.title: Store a Versioned Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Save [document] to [path] in agent-fs organization [org] and drive [drive]. Check the current version and use a concurrency guard when updating.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: save a document without silently overwriting newer changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find and Compare Related Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Search drive [drive] in organization [org] for [topic]. Summarize relevant files and compare the latest two versions of [path] without modifying them.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine scoped retrieval with version review.

prompt_templates.title: Join Stored Datasets
prompt_templates.prompt: Query [dataset A] and [dataset B] in agent-fs drive [drive] within organization [org]. Join on [key], calculate [metric], and report truncation and assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: analyze multiple stored formats with explicit scope and result limits.

output_examples.input: Explain how sharing a report differs between S3 and local storage.
output: S3 produces a presigned link that anyone holding it can use until expiration.
Local storage produces an authenticated application link that requires drive membership and does not expire.
Use the shortest practical expiration for presigned links and keep them out of logs.

output_examples.input: How should I update a document without overwriting a teammate's changes?
output: Confirm the organization and drive, then read the document and its current version.
Submit the update with the expected version and a descriptive version message.
If the version check fails, review the newer content before retrying.

best_practices: Confirm organization and drive scope before writes, searches, membership changes, or sharing.
Use expected-version checks for updates and include descriptive version messages.
Protect credentials and sharing links, and review privileged FUSE setup before approving system changes.
anti_patterns: Running sandbox setup commands unchanged on shared hosts or production systems.
Putting real credentials into command arguments, shared logs, or agent transcripts.
Assuming every sharing link is public or every storage backend supports identical expiration behavior.

faq.question: Can I use this skill with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes, the listing supports all three tools. Executing operations requires access to an installed and configured agent-fs CLI.

faq.question: Do I need Docker or S3?
faq.answer: No. The local filesystem backend stores versioned file bytes on disk without Docker or S3.

faq.question: Does semantic search work without embeddings?
faq.answer: Semantic results require embeddings. Hybrid search identifies keyword-only results when semantic retrieval is unavailable.

faq.question: Are generated sharing links private?
faq.answer: S3 presigned links grant access to anyone holding them until expiration. Local-backend links require an authenticated drive member.

faq.question: What data can I query with SQL?
faq.answer: The guide covers CSV, TSV, Parquet, XLSX, JSON, NDJSON, SQLite, and DuckDB. Database files require table bindings; results have row limits.

faq.question: Can I mount drives on every operating system?
faq.answer: No. FUSE mounting requires Linux, device access, and system capabilities. Review privileged setup commands before running them.
